evidenceAudit.scope: Classic, nodular and crusted scabies in adults, children, infants and pregnancy in India: diagnosis, permethrin, oral ivermectin, treatment of contacts and the home, built on the ICMR Scabies STW (July 2022).
findings: Clinical features, burrows, timing (3–6 weeks after first infestation, 2–3 days after reinfestation), permethrin 5% amounts and application, ivermectin 200 mcg/kg (maximum 12 mg) twice a week apart, crusted scabies regimen, nodule treatment, contacts and laundry measures checked against the ICMR Scabies STW (July 2022).
unverifiedSections: Benzyl benzoate, crotamiton and sulfur ointment are not in the ICMR workflow and are not dosed here.
Antihistamine doses are not given in the scabies workflow; cetirizine and chlorpheniramine doses are taken from the ICMR Dermatophytoses STW.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Scabies is infestation of the skin by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, spread by close skin contact, often within families, hostels, schools and orphanages. The female mite burrows in the stratum corneum and lays eggs; itch comes from a hypersensitivity reaction to mites, eggs and faeces, so it starts 3–6 weeks after the first infestation but within 2–3 days on reinfestation (ICMR STW). Crusted scabies in immunosuppressed, neurologically impaired or disabled people carries huge mite numbers and is highly contagious. All household contacts must be treated at the same time, or reinfestation follows.
keyMechanisms: Female mites burrow into the stratum corneum and lay eggs.
Delayed hypersensitivity to mite products causes intense nocturnal itch and papules.
Scratching breaks the skin and allows staphylococcal and streptococcal infection.
Impaired immunity or inability to scratch allows mite numbers to rise into crusted scabies.

symptoms: Intense itch, worse at night (ICMR STW)
physicalSigns: Papules and excoriations in finger webs, wrists, umbilicus, breasts, buttocks, axillary folds, waist, genitalia (ICMR STW)
Burrows: thin brown-grey lines 0.5–1 cm (ICMR STW)
Itchy nodules on male genitalia (ICMR STW)
Infants: face, palms and soles involved (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Crusted scabies: immunosuppression, neurological disease or disability (ICMR STW)
Pustules, crusting or fever: secondary bacterial infection (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Close contact with an infested person
Topical steroid use, immunosuppression (crusted form) (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Flexural, chronic, personal or family atopy; no burrows; contacts unaffected.
Grouped papules on exposed sites; no burrows.
Lice and nits in clothing seams.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Nocturnal itch with typical distribution and itching contacts; burrows are characteristic but often absent.
Mites, eggs or scybala from burrows or crusts, or on dermoscopy.
Thick crusts densely packed with mites, sometimes only on hands, feet and nails.

ruleIn.normalValue: No papules or burrows in web spaces, wrists or genitalia
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Papules, excoriations and burrows in typical sites
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Clinical diagnosis is usually enough (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat the patient
actions: Permethrin 5% from the neck down overnight; include face and scalp in infants (ICMR STW).
Ivermectin for poor compliance or poor response to topical treatment (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat contacts and the home
actions: Treat all family members and close contacts at the same time (ICMR STW).
Wash clothes, towels and bed linen used in the last 3 days in hot water and sun-dry, or seal in a bag for at least 3 days (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Repeat
actions: Repeat permethrin after 7–14 days, or the second ivermectin dose after 1 week (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: After treatment
actions: Itch can persist for weeks; continue antihistamine; do not reapply scabicide (ICMR STW).
Itch beyond 3–4 weeks or new lesions: reinfestation, usually untreated contacts (ICMR STW).
Secondary infection: treat per the bacterial skin infection workflow (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Crusted scabies
actions: Ivermectin on days 1, 2, 8, 9 and 15 (plus 22 and 29 if severe) with daily permethrin for 7 days then twice weekly, and 3–6% salicylic acid on crusts (ICMR STW).

medicationPlan.note: All scabicide doses are from the ICMR Scabies STW (July 2022); antihistamine doses from the ICMR Dermatophytoses STW. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

keyPoints: Permethrin 5% neck down overnight; repeat at 7–14 days.
Ivermectin 200 mcg/kg, two doses a week apart; not under 5 years or 15 kg or in pregnancy.
Treat all contacts the same day.
pitfalls: Missing crusted scabies in disabled or immunosuppressed patients.

patientEducation: Apply to the whole body below the neck, including under nails and genitals.
Itch may last 2–4 weeks after cure.
Everyone in the house must be treated together.
lifestyleAndDiet: Hot-wash and sun-dry clothes and bedding (ICMR STW).
Do not share clothes or bedding.
mdtReferrals: Dermatologist for crusted scabies or treatment failure
School or institution health team for outbreaks
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review at 2 and 4 weeks; new lesions after 3–4 weeks suggest reinfestation (ICMR STW).
